deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page works in a von Neumann algebra a on H with a faithful normal semifinite trace Tr, with P the set of its projections. An opening line, 'On suppose ... continu', is struck out, and the text then says the continuity assumption is not needed. For a positive (hermitian) A, φ_A(t) is the decreasing rearrangement ('t-th eigenvalue') of A relative to Tr. In modern terms this is the generalized singular value μ_t(A). The previous page used it to prove Hölder's inequality ||AB||_r ≤ ||A||_p ||B||_q and the Ky Fan type statements Φ_{|A|}(t)=∫_0^t φ_{|A|} = sup|Tr BA| and Φ_{|A+B|} ≤ Φ_{|A|}+Φ_{|B|}. The next page uses the results here to study a truncated Fuglede–Kadison determinant Δ_t(A)=exp∫_0^t log φ_A, including inequalities such as Δ_t(1+B) ≤ Δ_t(1+|B|).

Prop 1 (Courant–Fischer minimax in a semifinite algebra). The one-sided limit of φ_A at t equals inf over projections E with Tr E < t of sup over unit vectors x in (1−E)H of (Ax,x). The proof has two halves.
- One inequality comes from the spectral theorem: take E a spectral projection of A.
- For the other, one must show sup_{x∈(1−E)H}(Ax,x) ≥ φ⁻_A(t) whenever Tr E < t. Grothendieck reduces to A ≥ λF, with F a spectral projection, Tr F ≥ t, λ close to φ_A(t). It then suffices to prove: if Tr E < Tr F, then (1−E)H ∩ FH ≠ 0.
- Lemma proof: put X=EH, Y=FH, X'=H⊖X, Y'=H⊖Y. Then X⊖(X∩Y') ~ Y⊖(Y∩X') (Murray–von Neumann equivalence). In modern terms, the left and right supports of FE are equivalent via the polar decomposition, i.e. E − E∧(1−F) ~ F − F∧(1−E).
- If Y∩X'=0, then F ~ a subprojection of E, so Tr F ≤ Tr E, a contradiction.

Corollaries.
- Cor. 1: for arbitrary A, the same limit of φ_{|A|} equals inf_{Tr E<t} sup_{x∈(1−E)H, ||x||=1} ||Ax||.
- Cor. 2: φ_{|PA|} ≤ ||P|| φ_{|A|} and φ_{|AQ|} ≤ ||Q|| φ_{|A|}.
- Cor. 3: φ_A is monotone in hermitian A.
- Cor. 4 (margin): φ_{αA} = αφ_A and φ_{|1+A|} ≤ φ_{1+|A|} = 1+φ_{|A|}.
- Cor. 5: A ↦ φ_{|A|}(t) is (norm-)continuous.

Prop 2. φ_{|A|} = φ_{|A*|}, reduced to φ_{AA*} = φ_{A*A}. These are unitarily equivalent off their kernels via the partial isometry of the polar decomposition. The next page also checks it via Tr (AA*)^p = Tr (A*A)^p.

Purpose. To build, for semifinite von Neumann algebras, the full machinery of singular values and rearrangement inequalities (Hölder, Ky Fan, Weyl/determinant inequalities). This is the material of Grothendieck's Séminaire Bourbaki exposé no. 113 (1955), 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace'.
errors: One-sided limit: with the strict condition Tr E < t, the minimax expression gives the left limit φ_A(t−0) under the usual right-continuous convention. Example: A a projection of trace 1, t=1, gives 1, not 0. The proof itself uses φ⁻_A(t). So the label 't+0' is either a transcription slip for 't−0' or depends on Grothendieck's convention for φ. With the modern convention (Fack–Kosaki), one writes μ_t(A)=inf{||A(1−E)|| : Tr E ≤ t}.
'(fonction continue)' cannot mean continuity in t, since φ_A jumps in general (e.g. at finite-trace eigenprojections). It presumably means 'one-sided continuous version' or refers to continuity in A.
The sup should be over unit vectors x. This is implicit in the manuscript.
Transcription: Y' should be H⊖Y, not X⊖Y.
The proof of Prop 1 is sketched rather than complete. The reduction to A ≥ λF needs φ_A(t) to be approximated by spectral projections of trace ≥ t, which is fine but not written out.

ideas.what: Minimax (Courant–Fischer) characterization of the rearrangement/generalized singular values of operators in a semifinite von Neumann algebra with trace
ideas.modern_name: Generalized s-numbers μ_t(A) and their minimax formula
ideas.usually_credited_to: Murray–von Neumann (rearrangement in II_1 factors); Grothendieck 1955; Ovchinnikov 1970; Fack 1982; Fack–Kosaki 1986
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955), 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace' (content of the minimax statement there: unsure in detail)

ideas.what: Lemma: Tr E < Tr F implies (1−E)H ∩ FH ≠ 0, proved via the equivalence E − E∧(1−F) ~ F − F∧(1−E)
ideas.modern_name: Kaplansky-type parallelogram law / equivalence of left and right supports

ideas.what: Properties μ(PAQ) ≤ ||P|| ||Q|| μ(A), monotonicity, homogeneity, μ(1+A) ≤ 1+μ(|A|), norm continuity, μ(A)=μ(A*)
ideas.modern_name: Standard properties of generalized singular values (Fack–Kosaki Lemma 2.5)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fack–Kosaki 1986 (systematically); classical for matrices (Ky Fan, Gohberg–Krein)

ideas.what: Use of the rearrangement to define a truncated Fuglede–Kadison determinant Δ_t and determinant inequalities (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Fuglede–Kadison determinant, Weyl-type inequalities in finite von Neumann algebras

missed.claim: A 1953 manuscript proof of the minimax characterization of generalized singular values in arbitrary semifinite von Neumann algebras, without assuming the algebra is continuous. It predates Ovchinnikov (1970) and Fack–Kosaki (1986), which are the usual references. Grothendieck's 1955 Bourbaki exposé is published but rarely cited for this.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical attribution in noncommutative integration theory. The result itself is well known today, so the page would add nothing new mathematically.

deep.surprise_reason: Competent, essentially standard material, and it largely went into Grothendieck's published Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955). The only point of interest is priority over the later Fack–Kosaki framework; nothing mathematically new for specialists today.
transcription_corrections: In the proof, the bound is φ⁻_A(t) (left limit), consistent with Tr E < t. The 't+0' in Prop 1 and Cor. 1 is uncertain and may be a correction or 't−0'.
The marginal formula reads φ_{|1+A|} ≤ φ_{1+|A|} = 1+φ_{|A|}, consistent with the next page, not 'φ_{1+(A)}'.
'φ_{α(A)} = αφ_A' is the homogeneity statement (Corollaire 4) in the margin.
